rulings.challenge_claim: OL (high): the row's load-bearing recurrence claim is byte-false -- the two scene-turn runs it calls identical differ in their accents -- while the run that IS byte-identical sits across the row's own front seam and goes undisclosed; all three pointed runs re-collate at NFD. LF (high): the strongest rejected alternative locates its finer-cut rival at 'the row's fourth verse', a barred positional reference that is also numerically wrong, since the renewed scene-turn sits at the span's THIRD verse; plus the same three degraded quotes. The degraded-quote limb is ONE defect found independently by both; the recurrence limb and the register/arithmetic limb are DISTINCT and each holds.
rulings.grounds: TIER LIMB UPHELD: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא and קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.17.7 and בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at oshb:Isa.17.9 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while all three are self-labelled byte tier, so the row carries no quotation-grade pointed evidence at all. RECURRENCE LIMB UPHELD: the row calls the oshb:Isa.17.9 run 'the identical opening marker' to the oshb:Isa.17.7 run. Re-collating the SOURCE runs against each other, they are byte-DISTINCT -- the oshb:Isa.17.7 run carries munach then zaqef qatan, the oshb:Isa.17.9 run qadma then geresh -- and they match only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier, with the row naming no tier at all. That is load-bearing: the row's internal no-cut argument is that the aftermath continues as one row because the same marker recurs without an intervening closing signature (and no postpositive signature does fall inside the span -- 3 signature verses across oshb:Isa.15.1-Isa.21.17, at oshb:Isa.17.3 and oshb:Isa.17.6 and oshb:Isa.19.4, unit = verses, none in this span), so an unnamed tier is carrying the granularity decision. SHARPER THAN EITHER LENS PUT IT: the byte facts run AGAINST the row's own use of them. The accent difference at oshb:Isa.17.9 is the ONLY byte-level ground on which that site could be held apart from the onset sites, and the row asserts identity exactly there, while treating as belonging to different units the two sites that ARE byte-identical accent for accent. The false identity claim therefore undercuts the decision it was offered to support. FRONT-SEAM LIMB: fact upheld, inference corrected. בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא inside oshb:Isa.17.4 is byte-identical to בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא at oshb:Isa.17.7 and the row discloses nothing, but this is NOT 'the strongest byte-true rival to its opening cut': the row treats that run as an ONSET marker, so a byte-identical verse-initial recurrence at the row's own first verse corroborates opening there. What goes undisclosed is a three-site chapter series of which only two members are byte-identical, and the rival it raises is a larger composite unit with internal stanzas -- and it is the same seam-pair fact standing on the preceding row's back seam, so the cure is ONE edit across the pair. LF'S LIMB UPHELD EXACTLY: the rejected alternative places the finer-cut rival at 'the row's fourth verse' while the row's own rationale names oshb:Isa.17.9, which is the THIRD verse of the Isa.17.7-Isa.17.11 span -- a positional reference standing where a verse anchor belongs, and wrong by one. VERIFIED AND OWING NOTHING: the divine title at oshb:Isa.17.7 is genuine and is the only title verse between Isa.12.6 and Isa.29.19 (25 title verses book-wide, title-construct object, unit = verses); both cited marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed as setumah and correctly oriented, the segs standing after Isa.17.6 and after Isa.17.11 and so bracketing this span; one paseq seg is inventoried at Isa.17.9, count-only and single witness, and the row makes no claim depending on it.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) Re-splice all three runs from the source verse bytes -- the deterministic author-phase re-splice, applied class-wide. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'The identical opening marker recurs' with a tier-named statement -- the oshb:Isa.17.9 run matches the oshb:Isa.17.7 run at accent_stripped and skeleton tier only and is byte-distinct -- and re-argue the no-cut decision on a ground the bytes support, namely the absence of any postpositive signature inside the span, since an identity claim can no longer carry it. (3) device_notes: disclose the byte-identical pair across the front seam and state what it argues (both sites are onsets, corroborating the cut) together with the three-site series rival; author this as ONE seam-pair edit paired with the matching disclosure owed on the preceding row's back seam, not as two independent sentences. (4) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the positional reference with the verse anchor the row's own rationale already uses. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: each re-spliced run returns byte tier against its cited ref; every recurrence claim carries a tier named at write time and no run is called identical to another at a tier at which the two do not match; no positional reference stands where a verse anchor belongs; and the replacement no-cut warrant must pass the test that killed the original -- it must hold without the identity claim.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (low): the row's single Hebrew run -- its only quoted boundary driver -- is labelled byte tier but re-collates at NFD; every other claim in the row verifies. LF (medium): the same single degraded run. ONE defect, found independently by both; the lenses differ only in band.
rulings.grounds: The defect upholds exactly as the low-band lens frames it. ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים at oshb:Isa.17.12 re-collates at NFD tier ONLY while self-labelled byte tier, and it is the row's sole quoted Hebrew, so the row currently carries no quotation-grade pointed evidence. Everything else re-derives clean. The woe cry does stand verse-initial at oshb:Isa.17.12 (byte tier) and is one of the twenty verse-initial sites of that family (22 token verses book-wide, unit = verses), named as an ONSET and not blended with the indictment, self-exclamation or invitation roles or with the separate woe lexeme. The row's claim that the unit carries no oracle header of its own is correct: the flanking verse-initial headers are oshb:Isa.17.1 and oshb:Isa.19.1 (10 book-wide) and neither falls in the span, and the row discloses that it argues from the cry instead of from position between headers. No postpositive signature falls inside oshb:Isa.17.12-Isa.17.14. The closing seam is argued from the next woe cry ה֥וֹי אֶ֖רֶץ צִלְצַ֣ל כְּנָפָ֑יִם at oshb:Isa.18.1 (verse-initial in the bytes), so the woe chain straddling the back seam is surfaced rather than left silent. Both marks verify at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed as setumah and correctly oriented -- the segs stand after Isa.17.11 and after Isa.17.14, bracketing this span -- and the row's phrasing about the front-seam mark names the preceding verse, so the orientation is right. BAND CORRECTED: medium overstates. This is a single mechanical defect with a class-wide deterministic cure, on a row with no other defect, whose underlying fact is independently byte-true; holding it at the same band as rows that carry a second non-mechanical defect would flatten the calibration across this cluster.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. Re-splice the run from the source verse bytes as part of the class-wide deterministic re-splice, rather than re-keying it or copying it through draft text, which reproduces the defect. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref -- the test that killed the original -- and it must still be the verse-initial cry, not a widened window that reaches byte tier by other means.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (medium): the row states the mid-span divine frame arrives without a fresh addressee shift, but the addressee marker sits inside the row's own quoted run and two further address turns precede it; the row's own disclosed mid-span mark points at a rival its rejected alternative never considers; and all three pointed runs re-collate at NFD. LF (high): the same three degraded runs, including the ketiv/qere pair itself, which LF holds to the strictest fidelity standard. The degraded-run limb is ONE defect found by both; the addressee limb and the mark limb are OL's alone and they do not stand together.
rulings.grounds: ADDRESSEE LIMB UPHELD. The row's own quoted frame כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.18.4 ends in the dative אֵלַ֔י, which names the prophet as the recipient of that speech, so 'without a fresh addressee shift' is contradicted by the very bytes the row cites. Two address turns stand immediately before it: the imperative address לְכ֣וּ מַלְאָכִ֣ים קַלִּ֗ים at oshb:Isa.18.2 and the universal vocative כָּל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵ֖ל וְשֹׁ֣כְנֵי אָ֑רֶץ opening oshb:Isa.18.3 and closing on the second-person plural תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ (all byte tier). The frame is correctly owned as the divine one rather than the royal-messenger class -- that verse is a divine-frame site by inventory, and the royal-messenger sites are confined to the narrative zone. MARK LIMB REFUTED, on the challenge's own convention. The seg inventoried at Isa.18.3 stands AFTER that verse's words, so it marks Isa.18.3|Isa.18.4 -- precisely the divine-speech onset that this row's rejected alternative DOES weigh -- and not the vocative. Nothing corroborates a cut at the vocative: the inventory records no seg after Isa.18.2, this span's marks standing at Isa.17.14 and Isa.18.3 and Isa.18.7. Read with the after-the-verse orientation these packets apply elsewhere, the tier-3 layer SUPPORTS the rival the row already names instead of exposing one it missed, and it remains weak, single witness and non-driving in either direction. DEGRADED-RUN LIMB UPHELD, band corrected. ה֥וֹי אֶ֖רֶץ צִלְצַ֣ל כְּנָפָ֑יִם at oshb:Isa.18.1 and both כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י and אשקוטה אֶשְׁקֳטָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.18.4 each re-collate at NFD tier ONLY while all three are self-labelled byte tier. The escalation to high rests on the variant-note pair carrying the strictest fidelity standard; that is a register argument rather than a distinct defect class, and the degradation in fact lives in the pointed read-form, since the written form is unpointed in the extract and is a bare-consonant form mention. The row's variant-note engagement is otherwise a real strength that should survive revision: the doubled pair does sit in the letter bytes of oshb:Isa.18.4, the row names which form is unpointed and which is pointed, the note inventory carries exactly one note there, and it is the only variant-note verse anywhere in oshb:Isa.16.13-Isa.19.15 (49 such verses book-wide, unit = verses). Mark disclosure is otherwise exact and complete for the span at tier-3, single witness, correctly typed.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) Re-splice all three runs from the source verse bytes as part of the class-wide deterministic re-splice, keeping the written/read labelling of the pair intact. (2) boundary_rationale: strike 'without a fresh addressee shift' and put the byte-supported reading in its place -- the frame is explicitly addressed to the prophet by the dative standing inside the row's own quote, and it follows an imperative address and a universal vocative -- then re-argue the hold-as-one-unit decision on the ground that survives: the woe cry bounds the unit and the next unit opens at the following oracle header. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: keep the divine-speech-onset rival and add that the tier-3 seg standing after Isa.18.3 corroborates exactly that rival while remaining non-driving; do NOT add a vocative rival, since nothing in the marks layer points there. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: each re-spliced run returns byte tier against its cited ref; no no-shift or continuity claim may survive that the row's own quoted bytes contradict; and every parashah citation must resolve to the after-the-verse orientation and validate against the inventory under the claimed type at the MT key, single witness.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (low): the oracle-header run driving the row is labelled byte tier but re-collates at NFD, and the English sentence set beside the header is the line after it rather than the header's own rendering. LF (medium): the same degraded header quote, read as a systematic quoting defect rather than an isolated slip. The degraded-run limb is ONE defect found by both; the gloss-parity limb is OL's alone.
rulings.grounds: BOTH LIMBS UPHELD. מַשָּׂ֖א מִצְרָ֑יִם at oshb:Isa.19.1, the row's opening driver, re-collates at NFD tier ONLY while self-labelled byte tier, and LF is right that this is systematic rather than isolated -- the same canonical-reordering degradation lands on the other oracle-header row of this cluster. The header is byte-true where it counts: it stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.19.1 and is one of the ten verse-initial header sites (unit = verses). The row's other run holds: נְאֻ֥ם הָאָד֖וֹן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת re-collates at BYTE tier and stands verse-final at oshb:Isa.19.4 as tokens 11-14 of 14, and the row names the stacked title form AS the stacked form rather than folding it into a bare divine-name count, which is the right count-object discipline. GLOSS PARITY UPHELD: the staged folded verse reads “The burden of Egypt. “Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.” (web:Isa.19.1), so the English the row sets beside the Hebrew header is the oracle's first line and the header's own rendering is the short sentence preceding it. BAND HELD AT LOW against the medium lens, and the split between this cluster's two header rows is calibrated rather than uneven: this row JUXTAPOSES the English without labelling it, whereas the other header row explicitly calls its line the WEB header -- a false attribution rather than a loose pairing -- and this row still carries one byte-tier run, so it is not left without quotation-grade Hebrew. The row's remaining claims verify: the only postpositive signature sites in this stretch are oshb:Isa.17.3 and oshb:Isa.17.6 and oshb:Isa.19.4 (3 verses by inventory) and none falls after Isa.19.4 until well past the span, so the unbracketed-material claim is right; the tier-3 seg after Isa.18.7 sits on the front seam, single witness, correctly typed; the inventory records no mark inside Isa.19.1-Isa.19.4 and the row correctly leaves that absence as no evidence either way; and the mid-verse layout fold is held at tier-4 with the folded text used.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) Re-splice the header run from the source verse bytes as part of the class-wide deterministic re-splice -- a re-key or a copy through draft text reproduces the defect. (2) Re-cut the gloss so the English set beside the Hebrew header is that form's own rendering in the folded verse, with any following sentence retained explicitly labelled as the oracle's first line rather than left in apposition to the header. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref, and the quote/gloss pair must satisfy parity -- the English offered for a Hebrew form is that form's rendering in the folded verse, carried in curly quotes with an inline web: ref in the same field.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL (medium): the byform handling is genuinely right, but the comparison is drawn to a verse outside the span with no supporting ref while four in-span attestations go unmentioned, the cross-seam digit names neither swept object nor unit and is 'wrong on the obvious reading', and the pivot run is labelled byte tier while re-collating at NFD. LF (medium): the same degraded pivot run, which is the row's cited warrant for holding the counselors'-folly material with the Nile-collapse material in one row. The degraded-run limb is ONE defect found by both; the remaining limbs are OL's alone and they do not all carry equal weight.
rulings.grounds: STRENGTH CONFIRMED FIRST, because it must survive revision: יְאֹרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר at oshb:Isa.19.6 re-collates at BYTE tier, and the refusal to blend the poetic byform into an ordinary Egypt-name sweep is right. The hazard is live in this book -- a bare consonantal sweep on that skeleton returns 3 verses book-wide (unit = verses), and one of them is מִצּ֖וּר at oshb:Isa.48.21, a rock form standing beside a second rock token in the same verse and having nothing to do with Egypt. OUT-OF-SPAN LIMB UPHELD, and the operative rule neither lens names is the one that decides it: the row argues from 'this oracle's own header', i.e. oshb:Isa.19.1, a verse OUTSIDE its Isa.19.5-Isa.19.15 span, and that verse appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs, while every verse argued in prose outside a row's own span must be mirrored there. That is the defect. IN-SPAN-ATTESTATIONS LIMB DOWNGRADED to a preference rather than a defect: the ordinary Egypt name is indeed attested in 4 verses inside the span -- מִצְרָֽיִם standing verse-final at oshb:Isa.19.12 as token 13 of 13, and the name recurring at oshb:Isa.19.13 and oshb:Isa.19.14 and oshb:Isa.19.15 -- and an in-span contrast would have been stronger evidence, but the contrast to the header verse is byte-true on its own terms, since that verse does carry the ordinary name. That half is register-level strictness. CROSS-SEAM DIGIT LIMB UPHELD IN SUBSTANCE, CORRECTED IN FRAMING: the row's fivefold scene-turn digit carries no swept object and no unit, against the rule that a digit names WHAT it counts before it counts. But it is not wrong on the obvious reading. The sweep over oshb:Isa.19.16-Isa.19.25 returns 6 verses at skeleton tier and exactly 5 of them verse-initial, the non-initial occurrence being בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא standing at token 8 of oshb:Isa.19.21 -- and the row's own wording is about a series that OPENS the following material, so 5 is the correct digit for verse-initial onsets and 6 for verses carrying the phrase. The defect is the missing object and unit, not the number. DEGRADED-RUN LIMB UPHELD: אַךְ אֱוִלִים֙ שָׂ֣רֵי צֹ֔עַן at oshb:Isa.19.11 re-collates at NFD tier ONLY while self-labelled byte tier, though its verse-initial position in the bytes is real. The no-internal-frame argument itself checks out independently: no oracle header, woe cry, divine-speech frame, divine-speech-verb adjacency or postpositive signature falls anywhere in oshb:Isa.19.5-Isa.19.15. Mark disclosure is exact for the span (seg after Isa.19.15, tier-3, single witness, correctly typed) and the front-seam neighbour is unmarked, so nothing further is owed there.
rulings.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) Re-splice the pivot run from the source verse bytes as part of the class-wide deterministic re-splice. (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add the header verse the prose argues, so the out-of-span verse is mirrored; the contrast may additionally be strengthened by naming one in-span attestation of the ordinary name beside it, but that is an improvement rather than a required cure. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cast the closing cross-seam digit so it names its swept object and its unit -- verse-initial scene-turn onsets, counted in verses -- and states its tier, disclosing that the phrase itself occurs in one more verse than the onset count because of a non-initial occurrence. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced run must return byte tier against its cited ref; every verse argued in prose outside the row's span must resolve to an entry in the row's evidence refs; and every digit in the row must name its swept object and unit and survive re-derivation at the named tier.
